cases.name: A finished turn folds its work and keeps its reply
A turn with nothing to hide gets no fold
What survives the fold
A plan with text after it folds, and the wait for its answer is not work
A failed turn keeps its error
A stopped turn reads Stopped after, timed to the stop
A cancelled result reads Stopped
A stopped turn that said nothing is not folded: nothing would be left
A steered turn reads Worked for, and the steer opens the next
A delegator's turn waits unfolded on its sub-chats
A delegator's exchange folds around its chat cards and reports
A running turn is not settled; the one before it is
A question still waiting on the user holds the turn open
A window that cuts a turn folds what it holds, timed by the provider
A window that cuts a turn with no reported duration says Show work
Hidden prompts carry the exchange on; a schedule opens a new one
A subagent's own rows are not the turn's
Hours read with minutes and seconds
Supervibes: a turn left on an unanswered form shows whole, and the next turn runs from its own prompt

That one was cancelled as well, so nothing was saved again. This time the form asked for a Google OAuth client, with fields labelled the way Google Cloud console names them:

- `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`: shown as you type, with a hint that it ends in `.apps.googleusercontent.com`.
- `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`: masked, with a hint that it starts with `GOCSPX-`.
- `GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI`: shown as you type and optional, with an example callback URL.

Two cancels in a row may mean the form isn't reaching you. Did you see it and dismiss it, or did it never appear?

The chart is above: daily signups over 30 days, web and iOS. The numbers are made up for the demo.

You can switch between 7, 14 and 30 days. Hovering or dragging along the chart shows each day's figures, and the arrow keys step through the days once it has focus.
